newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FINLEY LEADS PADRES TO SEVENTH SUCCESSIVE WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FINLEY LEADS PADRES TO SEVENTH SUCCESSIVE WIN.

text.p: Steve Finley had three hits and four RBI to lead the San Diego Padres to their seventh win in a row -- a 7-5 victory over the Colorado Rockies on Wednesday.
Finley's biggest hit came in a three-run second inning when he lined a triple into right-field, bringing home two runs to snap a 3-3 tie.
He also had an RBI double in the first inning and a solo homer in the seventh.
Tony Gwynn extended his hitting streak to 14 games, going 3-for-5 to raise his batting average to .409, and scored twice for San Diego.
Dante Bichette belted a three-run homer in the first for the Rockies.

Colorado starter Roger Bailey (5-5) was tagged for six runs and nine hits over six innings to lose for the fourth time in his last five decisions. Will Cunnane (4-1) pitched six innings, allowing four runs and seven hits for the win.
In Pittsburgh, Dmitri Young had career highs with four hits and four RBI and Andy Benes struck out 11 over six innings as the St Louis Cardinals pounded the Pirates 10-0.
Ray Lankford added a two-run homer and three RBI for the Cards, who have exploded for 25 runs in their last two games.
Benes (4-2) allowed five hits, walked four and held an opponent under three runs for the seventh time in eight starts. He has struck out 35 batters in his last four starts.
Jason Schmidt (1-4) allowed two runs and three hits before being ejected in the second inning after hitting catcher Mike Difelice in the ribs with a pitch.
In Montreal, Tom Glavine allowed a pair of runs over 8 1/3 innings and Fred McGriff smacked a two-run homer as the Atlanta Braves beat the Expos 6-3.

Glavine (6-3) allowed seven hits, walked one and struck out six for his first win since May 18. Mike Bielecki gave up a homer to Chris Widger in the ninth but got the final out of the game to preserve the victory.
McGriff homered in the fifth off Expos starter Jeff Juden (5-2). Chipper Jones added two RBI for the Braves.
In Cincinnati, Chris Holt allowed one run over seven innings and Jeff Bagwell had a two-run double in the second as the Houston Astros beat the Reds 5-2.
Holt (6-4) gave up seven hits, walked one and struck out four as the Astros won their third in a row to move back to the .500 mark at 29-29.
Willie Greene hit two solo homers to provide the offence for the Reds, who have lost three of four.
Reds starter starter Dave Burba (4-5) gave up five runs and eight hits over five innings.
In Philadelphia, Frank Castillo allowed five hits over 7 1/3 scoreless innings and Ryne Sandberg had three hits and two RBI to the lead the Chicago Cubs to a 5-1 win over the Phillies.
Castillo (3-7) walked two and struck out five as the Cubs won for the fourth time in five games.
Garrett Stephenson (2-2), who had allowed just four earned runs in his previous four starts this season, was reached for four runs and seven hits in six innings.

In New York, Pat Rapp allowed a pair of unearned runs over eight strong innings and Charles Johnson drove in two runs as the Florida Marlins kept the Mets from taking over second place in the National League East with a 5-2 win.
Rapp (4-2) allowed five hits, walked two and struck out four as Florida held onto second in the East, 4 1/2 games back of first-placed Atlanta.
Luis Castillo and Jim Eisenreich added RBI hits for the Marlins.
Mets starter Dave Mlicki (1-5) allowed three runs and seven hits for the loss.
In Los Angeles, Juan Castro highlighted a three-run second with a two-run triple and Ramon Martinez pitched seven strong innings to lead the Dodgers to a 5-1 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
After Mike Piazza homered in the first for Los Angeles, the Dodgers struck for three runs in the second off rookie starter Keith Foulke (0-1) to extend their lead to 4-0.
Foulke gave up four runs and six hits in six innings. Martinez (5-3) gave up five hits and struck out nine.
Rick Wilkins got the Giants lone run with a solo homer in the third off Martinez.
